packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-02 -- unverified blind image reading (UTF-8 plain text)
Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this text. I opened only PROMPT.md and the packet images (the brief file was also read, as instructed).

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001, reduced overview, face A)
- Single narrow vertical strip of parchment/paper on black background, colour checker lower left, cm scale at right (strip ~5.5 cm wide x ~33 cm tall).
- Strip is cut from a larger document: text runs horizontally across the strip, lines cut off at left and right edges (both margins lost; words truncated on both sides). Upright orientation.
- ~33 lines of text in a single block in a German cursive (Kurrent / chancery cursive) hand, brown ink, occupying the upper ~2/3; lower third blank.
- Line 1 is in a larger, more formal display script ("...es Edlen Hochgelerten..."), i.e. an enlarged heading/opening line. Another line around the middle ("widerumben"?) appears written somewhat larger/heavier.
- Vertical fold or crease down the middle; small holes at top and near the bottom. Pencil note at the foot: "Stams, STA, Frg 58a" (modern shelfmark label, not text).
- No columns, no rubrics, no glosses visible. Tentative: vernacular (German) legal/charter text, not a literary/commentary layout.
- Tiles image-002..004 appear to be native-resolution views of this face (top, middle, bottom); image-005 is presumably the overview of face B with tiles 006..008.

FACE A, image-002 (native tile, top of strip; lines 1-14 of the text block)
Both edges cut: each line begins and ends mid-word. Hand: German chancery cursive (Kurrent), Bavarian-Austrian spellings (kh, ai, p- for b-). Virgules / commas used as punctuation. Line 1 in larger display script.
image-002 l.1: [cut]es Edlen Hochgelerten S[cut]          (display script; "Hoch-" written with ligatured c-h)
image-002 l.2: [cut]digen zubekennenden? herr?[cut]     (middle word very uncertain: z-u-b/l-e-i-n-s-?-n-d-e-n)
image-002 l.3: [cut]lligung. Ub? Fürnemen Ea?[cut]       ("Ub" may be "Vo(n)"; last letters uncertain)
image-002 l.4: [cut]rb, all(e)? Jnnamen? Ve(r)? stell[cut]  (abbrev. hook after "all"; middle word uncertain)
image-002 l.5: [cut]rechten, Redlichen, Satzen?[cut]
image-002 l.6: [cut]ren, Und verkhaufft?, Auch a[cut]   (verb: v-e-r-k/l-h-a(umlaut-like mark)-u-ff-t)
image-002 l.7: [cut]erb, Und allen seinen Erben[cut]
image-002 l.8: [cut]Paumbgarten, Darein ma?[cut]
image-002 l.9: [cut]macht? an die gmainig? ze? S[cut]    (third word uncertain)
image-002 l.10: [cut]rren, Und der Herren? Ech?[cut]     ("Herren" could be "Jener"; last word cut)
image-002 l.11: [cut]ch Verkhaufft wurdet, sam[cut]
image-002 l.12: [cut]hen, albegen? ain Jndr?/Jahr?[cut]
image-002 l.13: [cut]serrkhaiten?, gannz ve?[cut]       (first word ends "-khaiten"; beginning uncertain)
image-002 l.14: [cut]mehen? Jeger? alle Khauff[cut]     (superscript e/ü-mark over "Khauff")
Limitations: low confidence on lines 2-4, 9, 12-14; flourishes from descenders cross neighbouring lines.

FACE A, image-003 (native tile, middle of strip)
Overlap: image-003 l.1-3 = image-002 l.12-14 (same lines, not additional text). Re-read of overlap: l.1 "[cut]hen, albegen? ai(n) Jndr?[cut]"; l.2 "[cut]serrkhaiten?, gannz ve[cut]"; l.3 "[cut]mehen? Jeger?, all(e) Khauff[cut]" (abbrev. hook after "all"; "u"-mark/superscript over Khauff).
image-003 l.4: [cut]ner? ain gulden? ranscher?[cut]   (superscript mark over "Ner/Nar"; last word uncertain)
image-003 l.5: [cut]en, gannzwol benüegen?[cut]
image-003 l.6: [cut]gernet? Verkhaufften, hal[cut]     (first word uncertain)
image-003 l.7: [cut]ündungen?, Recht, Unnd gem?[cut]
image-003 l.8: [cut]llung, nun? Unnd Aus? Pa[cut]      ("Aus" with superscript mark: Aüs?)
image-003 l.9: [cut]und chain?, Lanzun?, Unnd[cut]     (middle words very uncertain)
image-003 l.10: [cut]s widerumben auch ob sin?[cut]   ("widerumben" in larger, more upright script)
image-003 l.11: [cut]andlen?, Khinn?, Undla[cut]       (uncertain)
image-003 l.12: [cut]Rechtenmacht Und gwalt[cut]
image-003 l.13: [cut]auch hinwaeg? für mi[cut]
image-003 l.14: [cut]Unnd fürstannd? Herrn?, [cut]     (last word uncertain)
image-003 l.15: [cut]n gewerscha[...] welchen? [cut]   (gap at stain/fold mid-line)
image-003 l.16: [cut]rgung? Unnd[...][cut]            (bottom edge of tile, partly cut)

FACE A, image-004 (native tile, bottom of strip)
Overlap: image-004 l.1 (cut descenders only) = image-003 l.13; l.2-4 = image-003 l.14-16.
image-004 l.2: [cut]Unnd fürstannd Herrn?, a[cut]   (re-read: same as image-003 l.14; last word could be "lernn"/"Erben", uncertain)
image-004 l.3: [cut]n gewerscha[stain]? welchen? g[cut]  (re-read: brown stain obscures 1-2 letters after "gewerscha")
image-004 l.4: [cut]igung Unnd von mein?[cut]      (completes image-003 l.16)
image-004 l.5: [cut]Oder schaden hinrangen?[cut]   (last word uncertain: h-i-n-r/w-a-n-g-e-n)
image-004 l.6: [cut]ren Durchleüchtigkhait[cut]
image-004 l.7: [cut]hündert, Unnd Vi?zen, S?[cut]  (looks like a date: "...hundert, und vier?zehn?"; numeral word uncertain; end of text block)
Below l.7: blank (lower ~third of strip), small hole, modern pencil "Stams, STA, Frg 58a" (last letter could be "n").
Face A total: ~33 physical lines of text (image-002 l.1-14, image-003 l.4-16, image-004 l.5-7 plus overlaps).

LAYOUT SURVEY, FACE B (image-005, reduced overview)
- Same strip, other face, photographed rotated 90 degrees (strip lies horizontally, ~32 x 6 cm). Pencil label at left end, written vertically: "Stams, STA, Frg 58v".
- Face appears essentially blank: no ink text of its own visible at this scale. Faint mirror-image show-through of the face-A text at the right half. Horizontal fold line along the strip, brown stains, small holes along the fold.
- A flat grey rectangle covers part of the right half (imaging mask/redaction placed over the photo, not part of the object).
- Tiles image-006..008 presumably cover this face left / middle / right.

FACE B, image-006 (native tile, left end of strip as photographed)
No ink text. Only: modern pencil "Stams, STA, Frg. 58v" (written along the strip end); fold line with hole; water/brown stains; faint show-through. Nothing to transcribe.

FACE B, image-007 (native tile, middle of strip; overlaps image-006 at left and image-008 at right)
No ink text of this face. Faint mirror-image show-through of face-A cursive at upper right (not readable as this face's text). Grey mask rectangle over lower right; fold line, creases, a few small dark specks near centre (ink spots/holes, not letters), stains. Nothing to transcribe.

FACE B, image-008 (native tile, right end of strip)
No ink text of this face. Clear mirror-image show-through of face-A lines running across the strip (columns of reversed cursive), unread as such; grey mask rectangle at lower left; fold with hole; stains. Nothing to transcribe.

SUMMARY / LIMITATIONS
- Selected areas: all text on face A (about 33 physical lines, image-002 l.1 to image-004 l.7). Face B is blank apart from show-through and a modern pencil shelfmark; nothing unread there.
- The strip is a narrow vertical cut through a German vernacular document (charter-like formulae: "Edlen Hochgelerten", "rechten, Redlichen", "verkhaufft", "allen seinen Erben", "Rechtenmacht Und gwalt", "Durchleüchtigkhait", "...hündert, Unnd Vi?zen" = probably a dating clause). Both line-ends are lost on every line, so each line holds only ~3-5 words.
- Readings are low-to-moderate confidence; the Kurrent hand with large flourishes makes several mid-line words uncertain (marked ?). No crops or contrast changes were made. A higher-resolution crop of image-002 l.2-4, l.9, l.12-14 and image-003 l.6-11 would help.
- Did nothing beyond the brief's rules. No exposure to any proposed identification.
